findings.title: Browser package makes an undeclared external Google Fonts request
mappedBasis: Model-plan revision 17 requires relative production asset paths and a portable browser build.
Phase 6 review scope requires local relative assets and no unexpected external runtime calls.
Demonstrable privacy and portability defect in the frozen production CSS.
evidence: evidence/browser-portability.json enumerates only index.html local references and failed requests; it does not account for successful external CSS/font requests.
stratton-presentation.md describes the production build as portable and says the only local references are the four index targets, which is incomplete for recursive runtime dependencies.
findings.risk: Opening the deck can contact an ungoverned third party, disclose viewer network metadata and fail in offline or restricted environments. The current portability evidence can therefore overstate the package boundary.
findings.remediation: Create a new sibling candidate that removes the remote import or uses an explicitly approved local/system or bundled font. Regenerate the browser package and evidence with recursive CSS asset inspection and a complete network-request receipt covering successful and failed external calls, then create a new manifest and obtain fresh AFF-A and AFF-B reviews.

mappedBasis: AFF operating contract confidentiality and unnecessary-exposure boundary.

findings.risk: The package unnecessarily fingerprints the authoring workstation and exposes a local account/workspace path if evidence is shared beyond the review boundary. No secret, credential or customer logo was found.
findings.remediation: In the new sibling candidate, retain only case-relative export paths and sanitise unnecessary PDF creator/platform metadata. Add explicit scans for absolute paths and document/PDF metadata before freezing the replacement manifest.
